To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a new approach for creating a POS-disambiguated lexicon of sentiment words for Twitter, (2) we propose word-level features for the classification of tweets into polarity classes that are based on POS tags, and (3) our lexicon outperforms the SentiWordNet lexicon in the task of classifying tweets.
we propose a method that combines automatically annotated tweets and hand-made opinion lexicon to expand an opinion dictionary.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new method for creating an opinion lexicon that is able to capture the informal expressions commonly found on social media, and which is also able to deal with ambiguity in word sentiment polarity, by providing a probability distribution for this polarity.
the development of a new lexicon that is able to capture the diversity and the informal expressions of tweets.
improving the quality and coverage of sentiment resources to support sentiment analysis of social media messages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method can be used to create lexicons that can be used to improve the sentiment analysis of tweets.
the lexicons created by the method presented in this article outperform existing resources in the task of classifying tweets into three sentiment polarity classes.
the lexicon created by our method is a valuable resource for sentiment analysis of Twitter messages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to build a Twitter opinion lexicons from automatically-annotatted tweets.
the proposed method is able to create lexicons that are more suitable for classifying the sentiment of tweets than SentiWordNet, which was created with a different objective.
our approach is able to capture the diversity and complexity of the informal language of tweets, and that it is a valuable addition to sentiment analysis tools for this type of media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of automatically-annotated social media data to create lexicons can significantly improve the performance of lexicons created from hand-annotated data.
it is feasible to create a lexicon for social media messages using supervised learning, even when only a small number of training instances are available.
the combination of information from automatically-annotat-ed tweets with hand-annotated opinion lexicons can be used to improve the quality of opinion lexicons for sentiment analysis.
